Design & artwork · 6 minute read

Preparing artwork for vehicle graphics.

Which logo files work for van signwriting and wraps, how colours are matched, and what to do if you only have a low-resolution logo.

Get a free quote ↗Try the Van Designer ↗

At a glance

4vector file types that work
1proof to approve
0printing before sign-off

In this guide

  1. Vector and pixel files explained
  2. What to send with your logo
  3. Colours, proofs and sign-off
Get a free quote ↗

Quick answer

Send a vector logo (AI, EPS, SVG or a vector PDF), your brand colours and the exact wording you want. If you only have a JPEG or a photo of an old sign, we can redraw it.

01

Vector and pixel files explained

Vector files are made of shapes, so they can be scaled to the side of a van without losing quality. Pixel files such as JPEG and PNG are made of dots and go blurry when they are enlarged.

Vector (best)

  • .AI (Adobe Illustrator)
  • .EPS
  • .SVG
  • .PDF saved from a design program

Pixel (may need redrawing)

  • .JPG or .JPEG
  • .PNG
  • Screenshots and social media images
  • Logos copied from a website
Tip

Not sure what you have? Send whatever files you have and we will check them for you before quoting.

02

What to send with your logo

1

Your logo

The original file from your designer, ideally vector.

2

Brand colours

Pantone, CMYK or HEX references, or a sample we can match.

3

Final wording

Business name, services, phone, website and any badges, checked for spelling.

For printed wraps, also send any photos you want to use at the highest resolution you have. Stock images need to be licensed for commercial use.

03

Colours, proofs and sign-off

Vinyl comes in set colours, so we match your brand colours to the closest film or print them to match. Screens show colour differently from vinyl, so we can show physical samples on request.

Before anything is printed you get a proof showing the layout on your exact vehicle. Check the spelling, phone number and website carefully: once approved, that is what we produce.

Low-res logo

A small JPEG goes blurry when enlarged.

Fix: Send the original file, or let us redraw it.

Typos in the wording

Mistakes are expensive to fix once printed.

Fix: Check every word and number on the proof.

Colours by eye

Screen colours rarely match vinyl.

Fix: Give colour references or ask for samples.

What to have ready for your quote

  • Logo as AI, EPS, SVG or vector PDF
  • Brand colour references
  • Exact wording, spell-checked
  • Phone number and website
  • Photos for printed wraps
  • Badges you are approved to use
  • Van make, model and year
  • Photos of the van

Before you book

Preparing artwork for vehicle graphics: your questions.

Can you work from a photo of my old van?

Yes. We can redraw lettering and logos from clear photos, then send you a proof to check before anything is printed.

Do you charge to redraw a logo?

Simple logos are often redrawn as part of the job. More detailed artwork is priced in your quote so you know the cost up front.

Can you match my exact brand colour?

We match to the closest vinyl colour or print to your reference. Send Pantone, CMYK or HEX values for the best result.
